Incident response team, we have a critical operational post-mortem and mitigation plan for the Kafka cluster partition leader rebalance failure during yesterday’s traffic surge.

First, examine `config/server.properties` to confirm that `auto-leader-rebalance-enable` is set to `true` and verify that `leader-imbalance-per-broker-percentage` is configured to one percent. Next, check `kafka-core/partition_assignor.java` and inspect `cluster-manager/controller.py`.

The primary root cause was an unexpected network partition between availability zones `us-east-1a` and `us-east-1b`, causing twenty-four brokers to simultaneously trigger leader elections across two thousand partitions. During the cascading election phase, message production halted because `min-insync-replicas` was set to three while replica lag exceeded `replica-lag-time-max-ms` of ten thousand milliseconds.

To remediate this cascade, we must tune ZooKeeper session timeouts from six seconds to thirty seconds and adjust `group-initial-rebalance-delay-ms` from three seconds to zero seconds for low-latency consumer group handoffs. In addition, update `cluster-manager/controller.py` to ensure that partition state machine transitions throttle concurrent leader reassignments to fifty partitions per second rather than unconstrained batch elections.

Under no circumstances should any engineer modify the `unclean-leader-election-enable` setting to `true`, as that would risk catastrophic data loss across financial audit logs.

The principal systems architect requires that all broker nodes configure `socket-send-buffer-bytes` to one megabyte and `socket-receive-buffer-bytes` to one megabyte to prevent TCP buffer starvation under high load.

Confirm that consumer applications utilizing the Java client library implement backoff retries using exponential jitter, starting at two hundred milliseconds and capped at five thousand milliseconds. Incident coordinators should also review `docs/runbooks/kafka_rebalance.md` to verify that manual topic partition rebalancing commands specify explicit throttle rates.

Furthermore, the observability team must establish automated Grafana alerts triggered when the under-replicated-partitions count exceeds zero for more than three consecutive minutes. Also verify that all broker nodes emit JMX metrics to Datadog, tracking active controller count and offline partition count with zero-second reporting intervals.

The data platform engineering manager confirmed that all storage volumes must maintain twenty percent free disk space before resuming high-throughput bulk ingestion pipelines. Network engineers must inspect edge load balancers to ensure TCP keepalive probes are enabled with an interval of thirty seconds and a probe count of three.

In addition, verify that consumer group heartbeat threads execute on dedicated high-priority CPU cores to avoid false positives during heavy garbage collection pauses. The billing ingestion pipeline must also configure consumer `max-poll-interval-ms` to three hundred thousand milliseconds to accommodate long-running batch database transactions.

Do not execute broker rolling restarts during peak business hours, between nine a.m. and six p.m. Eastern Time, without vice president approval.

All Schema Registry client libraries must enable local in-memory schema caching with a maximum capacity of ten thousand schemas to minimize HTTP request overhead. In addition, security operations must audit SSL certificate expiration dates across all broker nodes and ensure automated rotation thirty days prior to expiration.

Site reliability engineers will execute simulated broker failure drills in staging next Tuesday morning to validate that partition rebalancing completes in under forty-five seconds. The backup and disaster recovery team must confirm that MirrorMaker 2 replication lag between primary and secondary cloud regions remains below two seconds.

Furthermore, log segment compaction threads must be configured with `min-cleanable-dirty-ratio` set to 0.5 to avoid excessive disk I/O during active hours. Client application connection pools must enforce idle connection timeouts of sixty seconds to prune orphaned TCP sockets.

The platform security team requires mutual TLS authentication between all producers and brokers using certificates issued by our internal Vault PKI. Incident leads must also ensure that post-incident action items are tracked in Jira with assigned engineering owners and target completion dates within two sprints.

Regarding our upcoming migration to KRaft consensus architecture, please inspect `metadata/kraft.properties`. Confirm that `controller-quorum-voters` lists all five dedicated KRaft controller nodes across independent rack topologies. Verify that metadata log replication segment size is configured to sixty-four megabytes and the metadata snapshot interval is set to one hour.

All transactional producer applications must enforce `enable-idempotence` set to `true`, with `transaction-timeout-ms` configured to thirty thousand milliseconds. In addition, the JVM runtime flags on all broker instances must pin the G1 garbage collector with `max-gc-pause-millis` set to twenty milliseconds and `initiating-heap-occupancy-percent` set to forty-five percent to eliminate stop-the-world latency spikes during active partition movements.

Tiered storage offloading must be enabled for all historical topic partitions older than forty-eight hours, streaming compressed segments directly to encrypted S3 buckets. The data governance team mandates that topic deletion operations require dual authorization signatures in the cluster administration portal.

Finally, schedule a comprehensive architectural readiness review for Friday morning at ten a.m. with the infrastructure director to audit all verified configuration diffs and authorize rollout to the production cluster.
